q: Outsourcing the Jobs of workshops is resorted to when it is inescapable and under circumstances such as:

q: What represent the amount of expenditure, actual or notional incurred or attributable to a given product or service?
e: Option C (Cost) is the correct choice. because cost is defined as the amount of expenditure, actual or notional, incurred or attributable to a given product or service. It captures both real spending and imputed amounts charged to a product or job. Product and value are different concepts: a product is what is produced, and value is what it is worth, not the expenditure on it. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: The cost of selecting one course of action and forging the other is known as_
e: Option C (Opportunity Cost) is the correct choice. because opportunity cost is the cost of choosing one course of action and forgoing the other. It measures the benefit sacrificed by not taking the next best alternative. Sunk cost is past cost that cannot be recovered, differential cost is the difference between two alternatives, and joint cost is shared cost of common processes — none of which matches the definition asked.

q: In Management Information System (MIS) the top level management uses

The top tier therefore relies on strategic information.

q: What are the tools and techniques of Management Accounting?

q: Notional Costs are considered in

Financial accounting records only actual transactions supported by vouchers and does not recognize notional or imputed costs. That is why notional costs belong to cost accounting, not to financial accounting.

q: Allotment of whole item of expenditure or cost to a cost centre or cost unit is known as:
e: Cost Allocation — that is the right answer. because cost allocation means allotting the whole of an item of expenditure or cost to a cost centre or cost unit. The entire amount is charged directly where it is wholly attributable, without any sharing. Apportionment and absorption deal with dividing common overheads, so when the whole item goes to one centre, it is allocation. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: The process of distribution of overheads allotted to a particular department or cost centre over the units produced is called:
e: Absorption is the process of distributing overheads allotted to a particular department or cost centre over the units produced, so that each unit bears its share of the overhead cost. (Apportionment distributes overheads among cost centres; allocation charges a whole item of cost to a single cost centre.)

q: The Budgeting System designed to change in relation to level of activity actually attained is known as:

This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.

q: Responsibility Centers for the purpose of Budgetary Control includes:
e: The correct answer is AIl of the above. because responsibility centres for budgetary control cover every type of accountable unit. q: Management's reaction to a difference between budgeted targets with the actuals is aimed at whether:

e: Management has anticipated the variations — that is the right answer. because management's reaction to a budget variance depends on whether the difference was expected. If the variation was anticipated, no corrective action is needed; reaction is triggered when actuals differ from what management foresaw. Favourability, materiality and personalities matter less than whether the variance was foreseen. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.

q: Under 'Management by Exception which difference between Planned targets and Actual results should be analyzed and investigated:
e: The correct answer is Inventories/Material and Controllable factors. because management by exception means managers focus only on significant deviations instead of investigating every difference. Investigating all differences would waste management time, which is why this selective focus is the right answer. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded.

q: Section/Spending Unit of an organization for which separate budgets can be prepared and control exercised is known as
e: The correct answer is Budget Centre. because a budget centre is the section or spending unit of an organization for which a separate budget is prepared and control is exercised. A department is an organizational division, a budget committee oversees the process, and the final master budget is the consolidated plan — none of which is the accountable section itself.
